motion.$description: Semantic motion purposes. A component references a purpose, never a raw duration or easing, so motion reads consistently across surfaces. The CSS output ships a prefers-reduced-motion block that collapses every purpose below to 1ms; that block is generated from this file, so a purpose added here cannot escape it. `reduced` is the explicit escape hatch consumers select deliberately — it is the only path native platforms have, since they have no media queries.

page-transition.$description: Route changes and full-screen sheets — the largest move in the product.

list-item.$description: Staggered list and grid item entrances. Distinct from motion.state, which is hover feedback on an item already present.

progress.$description: Indeterminate progress rings, bars, and spinners.

celebrate.$description: Success moments. The only purpose permitted to overshoot, and the one most in need of its reduced-motion collapse.

fade-in.$description: Content reveals — cards, sections, tooltips, toast entrance.

fade-out.$description: Dismissals — toast exit, overlay teardown. Deliberately faster than the matching entrance.

loading.$description: Skeleton shimmer and other continuous loading states.
